verdicts.reason: All quotes verified verbatim. 17.01.04-confirmation-announce-gate.md:51 declares the precondition set 'all hard' and :61 C-06 makes a radius breach a block absent a waiver, reinforced at :277 (D-13) and :248 ('a hard permission check at confirm ... it is a blocking one'). 17.01.03-challenge-release-expiry.md:228 (D-15) states the opposite for the same moment — 'warn + override, recorded; never hard-block' — repeated at :142 and :201, while :109 routes confirm-under-challenge back through 17.01.04's gate ('Confirmation hands off to 17.01.04, which owns the atomic transition'). No file declares confirm-under-challenge a carve-out from C-01..C-06. The reconciliation layer contradicts itself inside a single entry: live-booking-settlement-cx.md:31 (CX-14) 'confirm (hard block)' versus :371-372 in the body of that same CX-14 section 'radius conflicts warn-and-override ... a hard block would be wrong'. Neither side carries a marker and neither owns precedence over the other (17.01.04 owns the gate, 17.01.03 owns the under-challenge path, and both ratify a D-row). 17.06-radius-clause-exclusivity.md:70 adds a third data point ('Breaching | A confirmed date breaches a live clause | Flagged') implying confirm is not blocked. Two implementers building the same screen diverge on whether a radius conflict with no waiver refuses the confirm or permits a recorded override — money and contract-breach behaviour, invented at the call site.

All quotes verified verbatim. 17.09.05-settlement-signoff-variance.md:67 ('Refuse | Not agreed | Undisputed floor moves'), :86 ('payable immediately') and :318 (D-09 'Refusal blocks finality, not payment') require funds to move on an unsigned settlement, and 17.09.06-settlement-audit-trail-disputes.md:267 (D-08) and :284 (Q-03 'RESOLVED — the floor is payable without a second signature') agree. 17.10.02-disbursement-execution.md:67 states the contrary as a state rule — 'Blocked | Settlement unsigned | Nothing moves; a proposal is not a payment' — with its Happy Path at :41 entered only after 'Settlement signs off ...; the number is final'. The domain CX sides with 17.10: live-booking-settlement-cx.md:23 (CX-06) 'Nothing moves until both parties sign — a proposal is not a payment', repeated at :179. Both sides are unmarked normative statements about when money leaves the platform, and each is written by the owner of its own half (17.09 owns signoff, 17.10 owns disbursement), so no precedence rule resolves it. 17.09.05:297 acknowledges the downstream file does not carry the input but is a cross-cut note, not an owner-and-target deferral. An implementer must decide whether a refused settlement pays anything at all.

Quotes verified (17.05.03-cancellation-tiers-forfeit.md:10, :25-27, :41-43, :100), but the gap is a data-shape gap, not a product-behaviour gap. The vision layer states the ladder's axis (proximity to the date, DT-02 at :81), its inputs (paid-to-date and days-to-show, read from 17.05.02, D-02 at :101), its provenance (authored in the contract, 17.04:97; live-booking-settlement-cx.md:131), the preview obligation with tier and clause (:42-43, D-01), the unfunded case (:53), the FM override (:32), the agreed-cancellation bypass (D-04), and the cross-collateralized re-tier (:56, Q-02 RESOLVED at :110). What is absent — tier count, boundary inclusivity, and whether a rung is a percentage of guarantee or an absolute — are per-deal authored values and a term schema, which is exactly what /write-architecture-spec and /write-be-spec produce. The closed-vocabulary argument also does not hold: 17.03.01-deal-term-grammar-types.md:78-89 is the settlement-expression grammar, and deposit amount + due date is likewise absent from it while being an uncontested deal term (17.02.01:49), so absence from that table is not evidence the term is forbidden. Two implementers converge on 'match days-to-show against the contract's authored rungs'.

The duplicate is real — 17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md:260 and :262 are both labelled D-14, out of sequence around D-13 at :261 — but nothing behavioural turns on it. Both rows state their rule in full and the two rules are unrelated (aggregate-only hold disclosure vs requests-lapse/holds-expire), so neither is ambiguous as content. The file's only D-14 citation, :148, quotes the decision text verbatim ('Requests lapse; holds expire — they are different clocks (D-14)') and is self-disambiguating. No implementer building from this file diverges: both rules get built. This is an identifier-hygiene defect in a decisions table, not a specification ambiguity, and the claimed forced invention ('which decision a downstream D-14 reference denotes') does not arise anywhere in the corpus.

The numbering observation is correct — 17.02.03-offer-approval-chain.md's Decisions table runs D-01 (:112) to D-06 (:117) — but the file tells the reader exactly where D-07 and D-08 live and states both rules in full. :123 reads 'Source: this file's D-07 (Edge Cases → "Band has never configured a rule") and `decisions.md` DEC-046', and :124 reads 'Source: this file's D-08 (Edge Cases → "Offer expires mid-approval") and `decisions.md` DEC-046'. The corresponding Edge Case rows at :70 and :71 carry the complete normative content (no implicit grace window, extension is explicit/pre-expiry/new-version; governance rule consumed from domain 01 with a fail-closed posture), and the sibling citation at 17.02.04:50 quotes the same rule. Nothing is missing and nothing must be invented; the decisions simply live in a different table of the same file than the ID suggests.

The collision is real — 17.02.03-offer-approval-chain.md:125 and :126 are both numbered Q-03 — but both rows are well-formed deferrals carrying an owner and a target (:125 'Agent | `/write-be-spec`'; :126 'Agent | `/write-architecture-spec` (01 ↔ 17 approval-chain boundary)'), and the two questions are about completely different subjects, so neither is ambiguous as content. The file's single in-body reference disambiguates itself by naming the stage: :73 `[PENDING — Q-03 → /write-architecture-spec]` resolves unambiguously to :126. Per the tracked-deferral rule, well-formed deferrals with owner and target are not findings; duplicate labelling with no ambiguous consumer does not make the tracking malformed.

Both passages exist as quoted (17.02.01-offer-sheet-composition.md:68 and :235; 17.03.01-deal-term-grammar-types.md:172 and :274), but what differs is lint-heuristic tuning, not product behaviour. Both specify the same flow: detect economic content in free text at send, offer Convert-into-a-term or send-anyway, and record an attributed timestamped acknowledgement that travels to the settlement sheet. 17.03.01's 'blocks the send' is a blocking prompt whose own copy at :172 offers '[It's not economic — send anyway]', i.e. the same acknowledge-to-proceed behaviour as 17.02.01's 'warn and require acknowledgment'. Ownership is stated, not contested: 17.03.01:244 delegates the firing site — 'The economic-content detector (D-09) fires at that feature's send action' — to 17.02.01, whose D-06 fixes the tuning target (≥95% recall, precision not optimised) that subsumes any specific keyword list. Keyword sets and a 40-character proximity window are detector parameters for a later layer.

Verified that 17.12-counterparty-relationship-payment-reliability.md:32-35 lists only settlement- and payment-derived signals and that no ladder-derived fact or fault-free code appears in it. But the missing content is enumerated in full, one file over, by the producers: 17.01.02:236 names the five ladder facts (hold→confirm conversion, request lapse rate as `no-response`, repudiation rate, flapping incidents, slots expired contended); 17.01.03:203 states the four exclusion codes verbatim as a 'Hard constraint on 17.12'; 17.01.04:250 adds confirm-then-revert rate as 'a new requirement on 17.12, surfaced here'; and live-booking-settlement-cx.md:35 (CX-18) and :482 carry the same list at the reconciliation layer. Cross-cut notes are the documented mechanism for stating a requirement on a sibling feature, and 17.12's own Behavior section is explicitly a two-layer model open to derived facts. Nothing must be invented — the vocabulary is written down, just not in 17.12's own prose.

Lines verified (17.13-fan-demand-signals.md:65-66; Open Questions :102-104 cover the Fan touchpoint, brigading and request→attendance conversion). The framing is also weakened by the feature's own gating question — :102 Q-01 is '[OWNER] Is a Fan touchpoint into live booking wanted at all?' — so a rendering constant inside a feature whose existence is an open owner decision is not a vision-layer blocker.
